title: Hosting a short-term rental in Joshua Tree: San Bernardino County permits, heat and water
summary: Joshua Tree STR permits in San Bernardino County, fees, TOT, Yucca Valley and Twentynine Palms rules, seasons and a desert turnover checklist.
body_markdown:
[All posts](https://prohost.ai/blog)


**Most Joshua Tree rentals sit in unincorporated San Bernardino County, which requires a short-term rental permit, a local contact who can be on site within an hour, and 7% transient occupancy tax. Yucca Valley and Twentynine Palms have their own permits and tax rates. The desert adds its own operations: summer heat over 100°F, homes on hauled water or septic, and guests who came for dark skies and quiet. This guide covers the permits, taxes, seasons and turnover work, with sources, as of November 19, 2026.**


## Key takeaways


- **Check which jurisdiction you're in first.** Joshua Tree, Landers, Pioneertown, Flamingo Heights and Morongo Valley are unincorporated San Bernardino County. Yucca Valley and Twentynine Palms are incorporated and run their own programs.
- **The county permit costs $1,144 for a new application** as of July 1, 2026, and renews every year ([San Bernardino County](https://str.sbcounty.gov/faqs) ).
- **The local contact rule is strict.** Answer 24/7, respond within 30 minutes, and be on site within an hour if needed.
- **County TOT is 7%.** Airbnb collects it, but you still need a TOT certificate and file quarterly ([Airbnb Help Center](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2469) ). Yucca Valley's TOT is 12%.
- **Spring is the peak, summer is the test.** March to mid-April is the busiest stretch in the park. Summer highs run around 100°F and can top 110°F ([NPS](https://www.nps.gov/jotr/planyourvisit/summer-seasonal-closures-and-restrictions.htm) ).

## Where we're coming from


We host in Hawaii, the Smokies and Joshua Tree. Joshua Tree is the market where the house matters as much as the location: guests book a specific look, a specific view of the night sky, and a hot tub or cowboy tub that works in the heat. Before ProhostAI I spent 6 years at Airbnb as a staff data scientist on the hosting team. Desert markets taught a clear lesson: what guests write about is whether the house worked in the conditions they arrived in, heat, wind or cold.


## The San Bernardino County permit


If your rental is in an unincorporated area, you need a county short-term rental permit before you advertise or rent for 30 days or less ([county FAQ](https://str.sbcounty.gov/faqs) ).


- **What can be permitted:** a dwelling. RVs, tents and yurts can't be.
- **How to apply:** online through the county's EZOP portal. The permit lasts one year and renews annually. If renewal isn't paid within 45 days of expiry, the permit closes.
- **Fees from July 1, 2026:** $1,144 for a new permit (application, permit and neighbor notice). Renewal is $550 with no changes, up to $1,144 with both physical and management or occupancy changes. Airbnb's help page still shows older fees, so trust the county page.
- **How many permits:** one per dwelling. A parcel of 2 acres or more can hold up to two; a smaller parcel one.
- **Occupancy:** based on the size of the dwelling, with a maximum cap of 12 (county, 2022). Your permit states your number.
- **Local contact:** must answer the phone 24/7, make contact within 30 minutes, and be on site within one hour if needed.
- **House rules the county requires:** no street parking, and a sign inside with maximum occupancy and the emergency contact.
- **Fines:** operating without a permit is $1,000 per violation per day. Citations run $1,000, $2,000 and $5,000.


We found no cap or moratorium on new permits in Joshua Tree or Homestead Valley as of this writing. A May 2024 county technical memo estimated short-term rentals at about 29% of Joshua Tree's housing. That's the kind of figure that leads to caps, so check the county's page before you buy.


### Yucca Valley and Twentynine Palms


- **Yucca Valley** requires its own short-term vacation rental permit, a business registration and a TOT certificate under Municipal Code chapter 5.40. Its TOT is 12% for bookings from January 1, 2023. The town caps permits; check the town's page for current openings.
- **Twentynine Palms** requires a vacation home rental permit, a business license and TOT registration. Local reporting in 2022 described a cap on the number of rentals. Confirm the current cap, fees and TOT rate with the city.


Neither town's site could be read directly when we checked, so confirm fees and rates with each one before you apply.


## Taxes


- **San Bernardino County TOT:** 7% on stays under 30 days (County Code §14.0203). Airbnb collects and remits it, but you still need a TOT registration certificate and must file quarterly ([Airbnb, article 2469](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2469) ). A November 2024 ballot measure to raise it to 11% failed.
- **Direct bookings:** the platform only remits for its own bookings. Collect and remit the TOT yourself on anything you book directly.
- **California has no state sales tax on lodging** , but you still owe state and federal income tax on the rental income. Talk to a California preparer. This is a summary, not tax advice.


## Seasons and demand


- **The park:** Joshua Tree National Park had more than 2.9 million visitors in 2024, who spent $179 million in nearby communities ([NPS, September 28, 2025](https://www.nps.gov/jotr/learn/news/2025-9-28-tourism-contributes-to-local-economy.htm) ).
- **Peak:** spring, from March to mid-April, when the weather is mild and the wildflowers come out.
- **Summer:** highs around 100°F, sometimes above 110°F. NPS closes some campgrounds and trails for the summer and has fire restrictions from mid-June to October ([NPS summer closures](https://www.nps.gov/jotr/planyourvisit/summer-seasonal-closures-and-restrictions.htm) ).
- **Winter:** nights can drop near freezing. Guests who expected "desert" arrive without layers.
- **Dark skies:** the park has been an International Dark Sky Park since 2017. A clear night sky is a big part of what guests come for.


For pricing: hold your top rate for spring weekends, use dynamic pricing ([PriceLabs](https://prohost.ai/integrations/pricelabs) or[Beyond](https://prohost.ai/integrations/beyond) ) through summer, and use midweek[gap-night offers](https://prohost.ai/features/upsells) when demand drops.


## Desert operations


### Heat


Summer heat is the operation. An AC that fails in July is an emergency, not a ticket. Keep a technician on call, service the units before May, and set a smart thermostat to pre-cool before arrival. If you have a pool or hot tub, check temperature and chemistry every turnover; heat changes both fast.


### Water and septic


Many homes in the area are served by small local water districts. The Joshua Basin Water District supplies Joshua Tree from its own wells, and parts of the Morongo Basin rely on hauled water. Yucca Valley is phasing out septic systems in favor of sewer connections under a state water board order. Know three things about your property: where the water comes from, how much storage you have if it's hauled, and when the septic was last pumped. Tell guests in the guidebook if there's a reason to keep showers short.


### Wind, dust and the drive in


Desert wind brings dust and sand into everything. Plan deeper cleans for windows, tracks and outdoor furniture after windy weeks. Many rentals sit on dirt roads. Say so in the listing and send directions that don't depend on a map app's idea of where the road is.


### Quiet, light and neighbors


Guests come for quiet and dark sky. So do your neighbors. The county requires an inside sign with occupancy and the emergency contact, and bans street parking. A[noise sensor](https://prohost.ai/features/smart-devices) and outdoor lights on a timer keep both groups happy.


## A desert turnover checklist you can copy


```text
JOSHUA TREE TURNOVER CHECKLIST


Arrival readiness
[ ] Door code works; backup code noted
[ ] Thermostat set to pre-cool (summer) or pre-heat (winter) 3 hours before check-in
[ ] Directions note sent; dirt-road / gate instructions current


Heat and water
[ ] AC running, filters clean, no warning lights
[ ] Hot tub / pool / cowboy tub: temperature and chemistry logged, photo
[ ] Water storage level checked (hauled water) and refill scheduled if low
[ ] No leaks under sinks or at the water heater


Outside
[ ] Dust and sand swept from patios, tracks and outdoor furniture
[ ] Fire pit cold; fire-restriction note in guidebook in season (mid-Jun to Oct)
[ ] Outdoor lights on timer and pointed down (dark sky)
[ ] Trash secured against wind


Inside
[ ] Standard clean: linens, towels, kitchen, bathrooms
[ ] Windows and sills wiped (dust)
[ ] County sign posted: max occupancy + emergency contact
[ ] Extra blankets out Nov-Feb
[ ] Guidebook current: park entry, heat safety, water use, quiet hours


```

## FAQ


**Do I need a permit to rent my Joshua Tree house on Airbnb?** Yes, if it's in unincorporated San Bernardino County and you rent for 30 days or less. Apply through the county's EZOP portal ([county FAQ](https://str.sbcounty.gov/faqs) ).


**How much is the San Bernardino County permit?** $1,144 for a new permit from July 1, 2026. Renewals start at $550.


**Does Airbnb collect the TOT?** Yes, the county's 7% on Airbnb bookings. You still need a TOT certificate and file quarterly ([Airbnb, article 2469](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/2469) ).


**What's the local contact requirement?** Someone who answers 24/7, responds within 30 minutes and can be on site within an hour.


**Is summer worth renting?** Yes, at lower rates, if your AC is serviced and the house handles heat. Tell guests what to expect before they arrive.


## The takeaway


Joshua Tree is a permit-first market. Get the county (or town) permit, register for TOT, and name a local contact who can really be there in an hour. Then run the house for the desert: AC serviced before summer, water and septic understood, dust swept, and a guidebook that tells guests about heat, roads and dark-sky courtesy before they need to ask.
